prompts.text: Who in this group would be most likely to turn a one-minute introduction into a ten-minute story?
Tell us about the moment a gathering of acquaintances began to feel like a circle of friends.
Let everybody introduce themselves with a funny fact or have someone else offer a friendly introduction?
Our group is asked to choose one object that symbolises how we met. What should we submit?
The friendships that seem obvious now sometimes started with completely unremarkable meetings.
The best icebreakers let people be funny without forcing them to perform.
What's the strangest coincidence connecting two people at this table?
Recall recognising someone in a new group after meeting them somewhere entirely different.
We have to make a documentary about this group's first meeting. Who provides the most unreliable narration?
A reunion quiz about our beginnings or a collection of stories from each person's perspective?
What silly test could we invent to see how well this group knows one another?
Describe a time two friends answered the same question in surprisingly different ways.
Guess everybody's childhood hobbies or predict their ideal day off?
Each person writes one obscure preference on a card; how should we match the cards to their owners?
Friends sometimes remember details that the people concerned have long forgotten.
Knowing a friend's boundaries is a better sign of closeness than memorising their favourites.
Which member of our group would probably surprise us most in a personality quiz?
Tell us about a friend guessing something about your habits that you hadn't noticed yourself.
A game asks us to predict one another's first reaction to a harmless surprise. What's the scenario?
Take turns guessing a friend's favourite meal or their most disliked household chore?
What's the most unexpected friendship you know between people with different personalities?
Recall seeing two people get along despite everyone predicting they wouldn't.
A lively friend who gets you out of the house or a quiet friend who keeps you grounded?
We have to pair up the most different people here for an afternoon challenge. What task would help them collaborate?
The funniest friendships often involve people who react to the same situation in opposite ways.
Compatibility can mean appreciating differences, not just collecting shared interests.
What difference between two people in our circle makes their friendship more interesting?
Describe learning to enjoy an activity because a friend cared deeply about it.
Our group has to choose a movie, but every person's favourite genre is different. What's the fairest system?
Let everyone pitch a new experience or let each person pick an old favourite in turn?
Which family member of one of our friends would fit into this group surprisingly well?
Tell us about being treated like family during a friend's celebration.
Share the funniest household saying you grew up with or the oddest family tradition you still follow?
Two friends bring different family recipes for the same dish. How should our group host a friendly taste test?
Friends who visit each other's families often return with new stories about familiar people.
Being welcomed into a friend's family shouldn't mean losing your personal boundaries.
What's a family custom you once assumed everybody practised?
Recall introducing a friend to a relative who turned out to share one of their interests.
We're invited to a celebration with unfamiliar traditions. What would we ask the host beforehand?
A relaxed family games evening or a group meal where everyone contributes something?
What's a playful habit that helps a group stay in touch without sending messages every day?
Describe a joke that survived years of friendship and several changes of location.
A monthly photo challenge or occasional surprise postcards between friends?
One friend is moving overseas and wants to keep participating in our group traditions. How should we adapt?
Some friendship traditions change format while keeping the same feeling.
A group can stay close without expecting everybody to be online constantly.
What kind of update from a distant friend makes everybody immediately want to respond?
Tell us about a reunion where the conversation picked up exactly where it had ended.
Our old group chat is recovered in twenty years. Which harmless running joke would need the longest explanation?
Plan one predictable reunion each year or make smaller spontaneous plans whenever possible?
What's one group-planning task you'd give to the person with the funniest taste?
Recall an outing that became memorable because the original plan fell apart.
A mystery destination selected by a friend or a familiar venue with a new activity?
Everybody in the group has a different amount to spend. How might we plan something enjoyable for all?
The friends who love organising don't necessarily enjoy making all the decisions.
A group's best plan is the one the quietest person feels comfortable suggesting changes to.
Who here would make a surprisingly good host for a themed evening?
Tell us about choosing an outing where two friends discovered a shared passion.
We have ninety minutes free, a small budget and no bookings. What would be our first move?
A city scavenger hunt in teams or an evening of board games and snacks?
What's the most light-hearted disagreement this group has ever taken far too seriously?
Describe a friendly argument that ended with somebody admitting they had misunderstood the question.
Settle our next harmless debate with a vote or let each side present a two-minute speech?
Our group is appointed a jury to decide whether pineapple belongs on pizza. Who volunteers as judge?
The same conversation can sound like an argument or a joke depending on how well the people know each other.
A funny disagreement stops being funny when someone feels cornered into taking a side.
What minor preference would you happily defend even while everybody laughs at it?
Recall a friend changing their mind because of an unexpectedly clever argument.
Two friends remember an event differently and neither has photographs. How should we reconstruct it?
An absurd debate competition or a round of questions where everyone can pass?
What small gesture from someone in this group has stayed with you longer than they realise?
Tell us about friends supporting one another without turning the moment into a big announcement.
A practical favour during a busy week or a cheerful check-in once the rush is over?
One member of our group has had an exhausting day but still wants to attend. How can we adjust the evening?
People often show care by remembering circumstances rather than offering perfect advice.
Giving a friend room to be quiet can be as supportive as a long conversation.
What's a kind way of recognising a friend who contributes quietly to a group?
Recall somebody including you in plans when they knew your schedule was difficult.
Our group wants to celebrate a friend's achievement without making them uncomfortable. What would you propose?
A collection of private congratulatory notes or a small shared meal?
Which personal boundary would make a silly but useful addition to our friendship handbook?
Describe a time someone respected your decision without demanding an explanation.
Ask before posting group photos or agree on a shared album where everyone approves their own pictures?
A friend accidentally shares an inside joke in front of someone who doesn't know its background. How could we include them?
Close groups sometimes mistake familiarity for permission to share personal details.
A running joke should retire as soon as one person stops enjoying it.
What's a considerate way to remind a friend about a social preference you've already explained?
Recall learning a friend's preference and discovering it was simple to accommodate.
We have a chatty group gathering and someone wants a quiet break. How should the host arrange it?
A clearly planned ending time for meetups or the freedom to leave at any point without explanation?
What shared memory would be funniest to recreate with everybody here in five years?
Tell us about a group tradition that began as an improvised solution to a boring afternoon.
Recreate an old group photograph or interview everybody about a favourite shared moment?
We're building a friendship time capsule with one contribution from every person. What would you add?
The stories friends retell most are not always about their grandest occasions.
A group doesn't need to meet constantly to create something worth remembering.
What's one future celebration you'd genuinely like the whole group to attend?
Recall someone joining your circle and changing one tradition for the better.
We get to establish an annual celebration for an imaginary friendship achievement. What would it reward?
Leave our next reunion date open to spontaneity or choose it together before we say goodbye?
